title: Unlikely that any properly divine authentic writing truly perished
source_text: IV. Attamen nobis non est probabile ullum scriptum proprie divinum & authenticum periisse. Nec enim id videtur statui posse absque magna providentiae divinae injuria. Ad quid enim Deus curasset librum aliquem divinum & authenticum scribi, ut tamen Ecclesiae nulli usui foret, sed statim Deus illum intercidere pateretur? Cumque inter eos Scripturae sacrae libros, quos divina providentia mirabiliter huc usque conservavit, reperiantur quidam exigui valde, & quorum non magna potest videri necessitas, quis in animum inducere poterit Deum fuisse passurum, ut perirent tot libri non minoris authoritatis, quique tales finguntur ut istos magnitudine, momento, numero & usu superarint? Adde quod Pontificii qui ἀδιαπτωσίαν Ecclesiae tribuunt, & supra modum illius authoritatem extollunt, non levem tamen hac in re illi contumeliam faciunt, & ignominiam inurunt. Quis enim posset tantam in Ecclesia culpam & negligentiam excusare, ut libros divinitus conscriptos, & ipsi datos, ut per eos instrueretur in doctrina salutis, illisque uteretur tanquam fidei norma, & regula veritatis, ut tales, inquam, libros, eosque multos, interire sivisset, nec ea, qua par erat cura, custodivisset?
pass_a_gloss: Yet it is not probable to us that any writing properly divine and authentic has perished. For that does not seem possible to hold without great injury to divine providence. Why would God have cared that some divine and authentic book be written, only for it to be of no use to the Church, while God at once allowed it to be cut off? And when among those sacred books which divine providence has marvelously preserved to this day some are found very slight, whose necessity cannot seem great, who could bring himself to think God would have allowed so many books of no less authority to perish — books imagined to surpass these in size, weight, number, and use? Add that the Pontiffs who ascribe ἀδιαπτωσίαν to the Church, and exalt her authority beyond measure, nevertheless cast no light insult and brand upon her in this matter. For who could excuse such fault and negligence in the Church, that she should have suffered books written by divine inspiration, and given to her that she might be instructed by them in the doctrine of salvation and use them as the norm of faith and rule of truth — that she should have suffered such books, and many of them, to perish, and not have kept them with the care that was due?
pass_b_english: We also doubt the premise: it is not likely any properly divine, authentic writing has truly vanished.
Providence is injured if God had a book written only to let it vanish useless to the Church.
Among books providence did keep, some are tiny and of no obvious necessity — so why invent larger lost equals?
Rome, which credits the Church with ἀδιαπτωσία and exalts her, still shames her if she let many God-given norm-books perish through neglect.
